title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 6th District
area: Baton Rouge and parts of south-central Louisiana.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map. This is an open seat: incumbent Cleo Fields (D), first elected in 2024, is not on the November 3 ballot.

candidates.name: Blake Miguez
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Senator, District 22 (since 2024); former Louisiana State Representative, District 49 (2015–2024)

summary.text: Blake Miguez is a Louisiana State Senator for District 22 and an oil and gas executive who previously served nearly a decade in the Louisiana House of Representatives, including as House Republican Delegation chairman. He is the best-funded Republican candidate for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District.

background.text: Works as an oil and gas executive; earned a bachelor's degree from Louisiana State University (2004) and a law degree from Southern University (2008).
Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 49 from 2015 to 2024 before winning election to the Louisiana State Senate District 22 seat in 2024.

record.text: Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 49 (2015–2024); now serves in the Louisiana State Senate for District 22 (since 2024).

candidates.name: Rick Edmonds
candidates.currentRole: Louisiana State Senator, District 6 (since 2024); former Louisiana State Representative, District 66 (2016–2024)

summary.text: Rick Edmonds is a Louisiana State Senator for District 6 and a member of the clergy who previously served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 66. He is running as a Republican candidate for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District.

background.text: Works as clergy; earned a bachelor's degree from East Texas Baptist College (1979) and a graduate degree from New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary (1990).
Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 66 from 2016 to 2024 before winning election to the Louisiana State Senate District 6 seat in 2024.

record.text: Served in the Louisiana House of Representatives for District 66 (2016–2024); now serves in the Louisiana State Senate for District 6 (since 2024).

Lindsay "Rubia" Garcia is a Louisiana educator with over two decades of experience who built a large social media following speaking about education issues, and is a Southern University Law Center graduate who interned with VOTE (Voice of the Experienced), a formerly-incarcerated-led advocacy group. She is running as a Democratic candidate for Louisiana's 6th Congressional District on affordability, infrastructure, healthcare and government accountability.

background.text: Worked as an educator for over two decades in classrooms, government programs and community organizations; served military families through the U.S. Department of Defense's Morale, Welfare, and Recreation program.

Graduated from Southern University Law Center with the Justice John Paul Stevens Public Interest Fellowship; interned with VOTE (Voice of the Experienced), working to restore rights for currently and formerly incarcerated people.
Organized community forums and boycotts after the 2019 Hard Rock Hotel collapse in New Orleans that killed three workers, and traveled to support communities seeking justice for George Floyd.

priorities.text: Says she is committed to defending the Constitution, citing her legal education and work with VOTE reviewing legislation for compliance with the U.S. and Louisiana Constitutions.

Emphasizes government accountability and checks and balances, summarized in her phrase "impeach, remove, imprison, repeat," for consistent enforcement of the law against officials who violate the public trust.
Focuses on affordability and expanding economic opportunity for working families, citing her own experience with financial pressure.

researchNotes: No candidate in this race completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey for the 2026 congressional race except Lindsay Garcia. Blake Miguez and Rick Edmonds, both current state senators and the best-funded Republican candidates besides Miguez himself, had no accessible campaign website content with specific issue positions; only their prior/current offices are documented. No campaign website or public statements were found for Monique Appeaning, Larry Davis, Michael Mebruer, Stephen Wagley, Rufus Craig or Patrick Forbes beyond their names and party affiliation on the ballot.
